title: Koppen's Climate Classification

cards.h: One code describes a whole climate
cards.b: Wladimir Koppen, a German-Russian climatologist, published his scheme from 1900 and refined it until 1936. Rudolf Geiger later modified it, so it is often written Koppen-Geiger. UPSC uses it to ask where a climate occurs and why, and to test map knowledge across continents.

Koppen used temperature and rainfall only, because natural vegetation reflects them. Each climate gets a letter code. The first letter gives the main group. The second gives the rain pattern. The third gives the temperature detail.

Example: Am means tropical monsoon. Cwa means humid subtropical with dry winter and hot summer.

A Tropical: coldest month above 18 degrees C. B Dry: evaporation exceeds rain. C Warm temperate: coldest month between 18 and minus 3. D Cold snow-forest: coldest below minus 3, warmest above 10. E Polar: warmest month below 10. A sixth group, H, covers highland climates.

Af: tropical wet, rain all year (Amazon, Congo, Indonesia). Am: monsoon, short dry season (Kerala, Konkan, Bangladesh). Aw: tropical wet and dry, or savanna, with a dry winter (central India, Brazilian plateau, East Africa).

The letters f, m, w stand for 'feucht' (wet), 'monsoon' and 'winter dry'.

BW is arid desert and BS is semi-arid steppe. A third letter shows temperature: h hot, k cold. So BWh is a hot desert (Sahara, Thar) and BSk is a cold steppe (Great Plains, Kazakh steppe).

Koppen used a formula comparing annual rain to temperature to separate dry from humid climates.

C: Cs Mediterranean (dry summer: California, Chile, Cape Town, Mediterranean coast), Cw warm with dry winter (north India plains), Cf humid temperate (western Europe, southeast USA).

D: Df cold with no dry season (Russia, Canada), Dw cold with dry winter (Siberia, Mongolia, northeast China). Group D exists only in the northern hemisphere, because the southern hemisphere has little land at those latitudes.
ET is tundra: warmest month between 0 and 10 degrees C. Mosses, lichens, no trees. EF is ice cap: all months below 0 degrees C. Antarctica and interior Greenland.

Strengths: simple, uses data anyone can measure, matches vegetation closely.

Limits: ignores wind, cloud and causes of climate. It is empirical, not genetic. Thornthwaite (1931, revised 1948) used the water balance. Trewartha later cut group C and D boundaries to better fit continental interiors.

India has six types. Amw: monsoon with short dry season (Malabar and Konkan coast). As: dry summer, rain in winter (Coromandel coast). Aw: tropical savanna (most of the peninsula). BShw: semi-arid steppe (rain shadow of Western Ghats, Gujarat, Rajasthan east). BWhw: hot desert (west Rajasthan). Cwg: warm humid with dry winter (Ganga plain). Dfc and E: Himalaya.

Likely questions: 'Compare tropical monsoon and savanna climates', 'Why is Mediterranean climate found on west coasts at 30-40 degrees?', 'Koppen's classification of India'.

  • Always give the code, the criterion and two regions.
  • Explain the location with pressure belts shifting seasonally.
  • Mention its limits to show critical thinking.

quiz.q: Koppen's scheme is based mainly on?
quiz.w: He used measurable climate data matching vegetation.

quiz.q: In Koppen's scheme, group A means?
quiz.w: A: all months above 18 degrees C.
Af is tropical rainforest, wet all year.
Warmest month between 0 and 10 degrees C.

quiz.q: Group D is absent in the southern hemisphere because?
quiz.w: Continental interiors at 40-60 degrees exist only in the north.

quiz.q: Koppen-Geiger is called empirical because it?
quiz.w: It describes climates without explaining their causes.

quiz.q: Coldest month below minus 3 degrees C and warmest above 10 degrees C is group?
quiz.w: D is the cold snow-forest climate.

sources: Certificate Physical and Human Geography, G C Leong
